record.textual_conclusion:
I3D architec-
tures have achieved better performances by employing a
ResNet backbone, as in the case of I3D ResNet 101 and I3D
ResNet 50. The SlowFast 8×8 ResNet 101 has achieved a
new state-of-the-accuracy 92.35% on the MS-ASL dataset
with an improvement of 7.03% higher top-1 accuracy com-
pared to the previous state of the art accuracy 85.32% in-
troduced in the MS-ASL paper that uses the I3D Inception-
V1 model.

paper.title: Cross Transferring Activity Recognition to Word Level Sign Language Detection
paper.citation: S. Radhakrishnan, N. C. Mohan, M. Varma, J. Varma, and S. N. Pai, "Cross Transferring Activity Recognition to Word Level Sign Language Detection," in 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW), 2022, pp. 2445-2452, doi: 10.1109/CVPRW56347.2022.00273.

sources.role: CVF open-access version of the paper; sole source of targets and protocol. No paper-owned code, weights, split files, or supplement were found.

locations: Paper PDF (all 8 pages): no code, data, supplement, or project-page link or footnote; no code/data-availability statement.
Web search for the exact title plus 'github code': only the Manipal research-portal entry and the ML Anthology entry for the paper; no repository.
GitHub repository search for the exact phrase "Cross Transferring Activity Recognition": 0 results; search for 'MS-ASL slowfast': no results.
GitHub account of the first author (Srijith-rkr, name and later affiliation match): 20 public repositories listed, none related to sign language, MS-ASL, or video action recognition.
not_yet_checked: CVF supplemental-material listing for the CVPRW 2022 ABAW workshop page
GitHub accounts of the other four authors
source_search.conclusion: No paper-owned code or data artifact found so far. The eight architectures and their Kinetics-400 pretrained variants match the GluonCV model zoo by name (see guesses); that is a cited-basis candidate, not this paper's artifact.

status.numerical_agreement_basis: Not assessed: no experiment was run and no in-scope target produced a value.
status.preference_level_basis: Provisional. No paper-owned code was found, so any attempt would have reimplemented training from the paper on published Kinetics-400 pretrained models. No implementation was carried out.

blocker.detail: The authors' hand-curated, hand-trimmed 50-class MS-ASL subset and its random 85/15 split are unpublished, and it cannot be rebuilt: 379 of the 1,109 source videos for the 50 most frequent classes are no longer public, leaving 44.2 clips per class against the paper's 48, with no way to tell which clips the authors kept. This is the earliest blocker and independently prevents all 24 targets; the under-specified training recipe (gate protocol-underspecified-training) is a second, later blocker.

metric_definitions.name: Top-1 accuracy
metric_definitions.implementation: Not specified by the paper. Standard reading: share of test clips whose true class is among the 1 highest-scoring classes of the 50-way softmax output.
metric_definitions.aggregation: Micro-average over all test clips. The paper does not say whether one clip or several clips/crops per video are scored.

metric_definitions.name: Top-3 accuracy
metric_definitions.implementation: Not specified by the paper. Standard reading: share of test clips whose true class is among the 3 highest-scoring classes of the 50-way softmax output.
metric_definitions.aggregation: Micro-average over all test clips. The paper does not say whether one clip or several clips/crops per video are scored.

metric_definitions.name: Top-5 accuracy
metric_definitions.implementation: Not specified by the paper. Standard reading: share of test clips whose true class is among the 5 highest-scoring classes of the 50-way softmax output.
metric_definitions.aggregation: Micro-average over all test clips. The paper does not say whether one clip or several clips/crops per video are scored.

experiments.system: P3D pretrained on Kinetics-400 and fine-tuned for 50-way classification (25M parameters, 32 input frames per Table 2)
experiments.protocol: Sec. 4.2: train the new output layer at lr 1e-2 for 20 epochs, then unfreeze and tune 'until we achieved optimal performance for each model'; cosine schedule between 1e-2 and 1e-5; L2 weight decay between 1e-3 and 1e-4; Adam; softmax cross-entropy; horizontal flip, scale ratios in (1.0, 0.8), random crop 224x224; 64 consecutive frames sampled per clip.
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Not specified. No validation split is described; test accuracy is reported after per-model tuning.
experiments.seed_policy: Not specified; single reported value per cell.
experiments.dataset_note: Run by the authors on their curated 50-class subset of this dataset, which was never obtained.

guesses.detail: The paper names no framework or weight source. The eight systems (P3D, R(2+1)D at 112x112, I3D InceptionV3, I3D ResNet 50/101, SlowFast 4x16 R50, 8x8 R50, 8x8 R101, all Kinetics-400 pretrained) coincide with entries of the GluonCV action-recognition model zoo. Treated as the leading candidate basis; backbone depth for P3D and R(2+1)D is inferred from that match and the Table 2 parameter counts, not stated by the paper. Not yet verified against the zoo's parameter counts.

gates.reason: The Modal wrapper preflight failed on 2026-10-02: "Modal credentials for 'repro-sign' are invalid or expired." No Modal volume, app, or billing state was inspected.
evidence: Output of .agents/skills/reproduce-paper/scripts/modal_repro_sign.sh volume list --json on 2026-10-02.
gates.required_action: The user runs `modal setup` and selects the repro-sign workspace; then re-run the wrapper preflight and check_modal_dataset.sh for MS-ASL.
gates.resolution: Resolved 2026-10-02. The user re-ran `modal setup`; the wrapper still failed because the installed Modal CLI 1.2.6 (Python 3.9) has no `modal token info` command, which the wrapper uses for its workspace check. With Modal CLI 1.6.0 installed in a separate Python 3.13 venv and placed first on PATH, the wrapper preflight printed "Verified Modal profile and workspace 'repro-sign'."

gates.reason: Every Table 2 number was measured on the authors' own hand-curated, hand-trimmed 50-class subset of MS-ASL with a random 85/15 split. Neither the clip list, the trims, nor the split is published, and the paper itself says the set deviates from MS-ASL because many links were dead.
evidence: Sec. 4.1: 'we chose the 50 classes with the highest frequency'; 'Videos from these classes were manually downloaded, screened, and trimmed'; 'Our compiled dataset deviated from the original MS-ASL dataset as a significant amount of video links were no longer valid'; 'each class has 48 videos on average, with a standard deviation of 6'; 'Videos were split into 85% and 15% train-test split.'
No data-availability statement, split file, or seed anywhere in the paper; source search found no artifact.
Queue dataset record names plain 'MS-ASL' with available 'yes'; that identifies the parent dataset, not the experiment's data.
Modal check on 2026-10-02: no MS-ASL directory exists in Volume `datasets` (26 root directories listed), so neither the authors' subset nor the parent dataset is on project storage.

Official MS-ASL annotations (MS-ASL.zip from download.microsoft.com, sha256 a8562008309eea4129e1bc0ed7f654a314fee195227222859657e307b6434c34, C-UDA 0.1): 25,513 clips over 7,212 YouTube videos. The Zenodo MS-ASL.zip in the queue record (record 6674324) is OpenHands pose data, not video.

Top-50 classes from annotations alone (train+val+test clip counts): labels 0-49 hold 3,191 clips over 1,109 videos (56-85 per class). The cut is tied: 'bored', 'help' (label 50), 'water', 'computer' and 'boy' all have 56 clips for the last four places, so 'the 50 most frequent classes' is label<50 or a variant swapping 'help' in. The paper names 'water' and 'computer' among its classes.

Availability on 2026-10-02 via YouTube's public oEmbed endpoint for those 1,109 videos: 730 public (HTTP 200), 194 removed (404), 169 private (403), 16 embedding-restricted (401, playability unknown). On the 40 videos also attempted with yt-dlp the two agree (25/25 downloaded = 200; 15/15 unavailable = 403/404). Clips on public videos: 2,208 of 3,191 (69.2%): train 1,537, val 372, test 299; per class mean 44.2, SD 5.6, range 31-56; 115 of 165 signers. The paper reports mean 48, SD 6 per class after its own screening.

Bulk video download from the cluster was stopped on 2026-10-02 after 223 of 7,212 videos when YouTube began requiring sign-in bot verification; it was not worked around. 25 of the 730 public top-50 videos are already staged.

Check of the paper's '48 videos on average, SD 6' against labels 0-49 (2026-10-02). Per-class clips: full 2019 release 63.8, SD 6.2 (total 3,191); public today 44.2, SD 5.6 (2,208), or 46.0, SD 5.5 (2,301) counting embed-restricted videos. Per-class distinct source videos: full release 50.9, SD 6.0 (2,545); public today 34.9, SD 5.1. No reading available today gives 48: the paper's figure sits between the full release and today's public set if 'videos' means clips (about 75% of the release), or just under the full release if it means distinct source videos (about 94%). The statistic is consistent with a top-50 subset but cannot be verified, and does not identify which clips the authors kept.

gates.reason: Beyond the data, the fine-tuning recipe is not reproducible as written: per-model hyperparameters were tuned 'until we achieved optimal performance' with only ranges given, and there is no validation split, so the reported test accuracy is also the model-selection criterion.
evidence: Sec. 4.2: 'We then began unfreezing the network architecture and hyperparameter tuning until we achieved optimal performance for each model.'

Sec. 4.2 gives ranges only: cosine schedule 1e-2 to 1e-5; weight decay 1e-3 to 1e-4. Batch size, epochs after unfreezing, unfreezing order, framework, pretrained-weight source, test-time clip sampling, and seeds are not stated.
Sec. 4.1 describes only a train/test split.
gates.required_action: If a run is authorised under the data gate, agree one fixed, documented recipe per model before launch (no tuning against the test split); record every filled-in value as a guess.
gates.resolution: Not reached: closed 2026-10-02 without a decision because the data blocker ended the attempt before any recipe was needed. The under-specification stands as recorded.

datasets.name: MS-ASL (parent of the authors' unpublished curated 50-class subset)
datasets.version_or_subset: Official 2019 annotation release (MS-ASL.zip, sha256 a8562008309eea4129e1bc0ed7f654a314fee195227222859657e307b6434c34): 25,513 clips over 7,212 YouTube videos, 1,000 classes. The experiments used a derived set that is not this release: Unpublished. Sec. 4.1: the 50 most frequent MS-ASL classes; videos 'manually downloaded, screened, and trimmed'; repeated signs, non-target-class frames and idle frames removed by hand; long clips uniformly subsampled, short clips zero-padded at the front; about 48 videos per class (std 6), i.e. roughly 2,400 clips; random 85%/15% train/test split with no published file list or seed.
datasets.license_or_permission: Queue record lists MS-ASL under Microsoft's Computational Use of Data Agreement (C-UDA); that covers the annotation files. The underlying videos are third-party YouTube uploads and the authors' curated clips are author-held. Not yet verified for project-cloud processing.
datasets.cloud_processing_basis: Unresolved and treated as not allowed for the videos: C-UDA covers the annotations only, and no decision was recorded on storing third-party YouTube videos on project storage beyond the assignee's instruction to attempt acquisition. Nothing was uploaded.
datasets.populated_note: Checked 2026-10-02 through the wrapper (Modal CLI 1.6.0, profile repro-sign). Volumes `datasets` and `huggingface-cache` both exist. The `datasets` root has 26 directories and none is MS-ASL or a derivative: `check_modal_dataset.sh ms-asl` exited 1 with "Requested dataset 'ms-asl' is absent from Modal Volume 'datasets'", and a case-insensitive listing for 'asl' matched only WLASL, arasl-database-grayscale, asl-alphabet, asl-citizen, asl-semcom-rgb, and aslg-pc12, which are different datasets. The path is the intended slug only.
datasets.availability: Exact data unavailable from public sources: the clip list, manual trims, and split are unpublished (gate data-authors-curated-subset).
datasets.expected_counts: About 2,400 clips over 50 classes; test split about 15% (about 360 clips). Exact counts are not stated in the paper.

dead_ends.detail: data.sh was run on 2026-10-02 from an institutional cluster to build a shared ms-asl tree (official annotations plus one clip per annotation). It processed 223 of 7,212 videos (126 downloaded, 349 clips cut; 97 private or removed) in two minutes, then stopped when YouTube required sign-in bot verification, which was not worked around. Nothing was uploaded to Modal. Earlier HTTP 403 failures were a tooling fault fixed by installing a current yt-dlp with a JavaScript runtime.
